package_info.package_manager: N/A (open-source Android malware, not distributed via official package manager)
package_info.package_versions: All known versions as of June 2024
package_info.why_malicious: Rafel RAT is a remote administration tool explicitly designed for malicious use, providing attackers with full remote control over Android devices. It enables unauthorized access to sensitive data, surveillance through device sensors, remote command execution, and ransomware deployment. Its documented use in targeted espionage and cybercrime campaigns against individuals and organizations demonstrates its high threat level and intent.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after installation, upon device boot or app launch)
execution_context.file_location: Main RAT payload (Android APK main activity/service)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The RAT requests and abuses Android permissions to access contacts, SMS, call logs, camera, microphone, and file storage, then exfiltrates this data to a remote C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after installation or device boot, the code abuses granted Android permissions to collect sensitive user data (contacts, SMS, call logs, files, camera/microphone recordings), then transmits this data via HTTP/S POST requests to a remote command-and-control server, enabling covert espionage and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects a wide range of sensitive user data and silently exfiltrates it to an external server without user consent, which is a hallmark of spyware and RATs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Android apps only request permissions necessary for their stated function and do not silently collect and transmit user data in the background.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise mobile device management (MDM) tools may request similar permissions, but only with explicit user or organizational consent and clear notification.
key_indicators: Abuse of multiple sensitive Android permissions (contacts, SMS, call logs, camera, microphone, storage, location, device admin)
Silent background data exfiltration to remote C2 server
Operation triggered on device boot or app launch without user interaction
Use of HTTP/S POST requests to transmit user data externally

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on C2 command or scheduled task)
execution_context.file_location: RAT command handler (background service within APK)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Implements remote command execution, file upload/download, and device control (e.g., lock device, wipe data, install/uninstall apps) via commands received from the C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving commands from the C2 server, the code executes arbitrary actions on the device, such as uploading or downloading files, locking or wiping the device, and installing or uninstalling applications, thereby granting the attacker persistent and full remote control over the device.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote command execution and device control capabilities are typical of RAT malware and are not present in legitimate consumer applications.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not allow remote parties to execute arbitrary commands or manipulate device security features such as locking, wiping, or app management.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Mobile device management (MDM) solutions may have similar capabilities, but only with explicit user or enterprise consent and strict policy controls.
key_indicators: Remote command execution via C2 communication
Device lock and wipe functionality triggered remotely
Unsolicited installation or uninstallation of applications
Background service listening for and executing C2 instructions

execution_context.file_location: RAT ransomware module (within APK or loaded dynamically)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Encrypts user files on the device and displays a ransom note, demanding payment for decryption.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a ransomware activation command from the C2 server, the code encrypts user files on the device and displays a ransom note to the user, coercing the victim to pay a ransom for file decryption and data recovery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs unauthorized file encryption and displays a ransom demand, which are definitive indicators of ransomware activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications never encrypt user files for ransom or demand payment to restore access.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for this behavior in consumer or enterprise apps.
key_indicators: File encryption without user consent or notification
Display of ransom note demanding payment for decryption
Destructive modification of user data triggered by remote command

attack_chain.action: Victim installs the malicious APK (Rafel RAT) on their Android device, typically via social engineering, phishing, or trojanized app distribution outside official app stores.
RAT requests and abuses sensitive Android permissions to access user data and device features, often disguising its intent during installation.
RAT collects sensitive data (contacts, SMS, call logs, files, camera/microphone recordings) and exfiltrates it to the attacker's C2 server using covert network communications.
RAT receives and executes remote commands from the C2 server, enabling full device control including file operations, device lock/wipe, and app management.
RAT activates its ransomware module to encrypt user files and display a ransom note, if instructed by the attacker via C2 command.

behavioral_signatures: Android application requesting an excessive set of sensitive permissions (contacts, SMS, call logs, camera, microphone, device admin, storage, location, boot receiver)
Background network connections to hardcoded or dynamically resolved C2 domains/IPs
Silent exfiltration of user data (contacts, SMS, call logs, files, recordings) without user interaction or notification
Remote command execution and device control actions (lock, wipe, app install/uninstall) initiated from external servers
File encryption activity and display of ransom note to the user
file_indicators: APK files with obfuscated code and suspicious permission requests in AndroidManifest.xml
Presence of device admin receiver components declared in the manifest
Unusual background services registered to start on boot (RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED)
Embedded or dynamically loaded modules for ransomware functionality
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/S connections to known or suspicious C2 domains/IPs hardcoded or resolved at runtime
Unusual HTTP/S POST requests containing device or user data payloads
Regular beaconing behavior to remote servers after installation, even when app is not in foreground
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android applications that request a broad and atypical set of sensitive permissions, especially device admin rights and boot receivers. Analyze app behavior for silent data exfiltration, remote command execution, and file encryption activities. Use network monitoring to detect outbound connections to known or suspicious C2 infrastructure and inspect for HTTP/S POST requests containing user data. Look for the presence of ransom note artifacts and abnormal file access or modification patterns. Employ mobile security solutions capable of both static code analysis (for permission abuse and obfuscated code) and dynamic behavioral analysis (for RAT and ransomware indicators).
